extracted.intended_audience: math teachers and math content creators (participants or potential reviewers for the Summer of Math Exposition)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creators submitting entries to the Summer of Math Exposition and for teachers who might review them; emphasizes choosing topics and presentations that are helpful to students and inviting teachers to provide feedback that will influence prizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teacher-assessed helpfulness to students
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether teachers of the relevant subject believe the entry would be helpful to their students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant: "in giving out cash prizes to 5 entries this year, I’ll be placing heavy weight on whether teachers of the relevant subject believe the entry would be helpful to their students." Teachers' judgments will be a major factor in prize selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose topics based on student helpfulness (not only peer appeal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer topics selected because they will help students, rather than topics chosen primarily to please math enthusiasts who participate in peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page text: "A risk... is that the entries which is most rewarded are lessons that appeal to those already very passionate about math... I would love to be able to re-direct the enormous amount of creative energy ... to encourage people to choose topics not just based on what fellow math-nerds will love, but based on what will be most helpful."

rubrics_metrics.name: Address topics that are especially hard to explain to students
rubrics_metrics.description: Target subjects that teachers find difficult to explain in class and that students struggle to understand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt to teachers: "What is especially hard to explain to students?" — creators are encouraged to tackle these harder-to-explain topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use visualizations and better narratives where useful
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries should employ visualizations or improved narrative exposition when those approaches would aid student understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page asks: "Where would visualizations or better narratives be especially useful?" Encourages creators to consider visual and narrative approaches to improve pedagogy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fill gaps where existing online resources disappoint
rubrics_metrics.description: Create content that addresses topics or explanations for which search results currently leave teachers or students disappointed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page asks teachers: "What have you searched for where the results you got left you disappointed?" — indicating a preference for entries that meet unmet demand or poor-quality existing coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with the peer review process to gain exposure and community feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating in the event's peer review period is valuable for exposing new creators and surfacing diverse topics and perspectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "One of the great joys of the Summer of Math Exposition is that through the peer review process, we have a flood of activity... that helps new creators gain exposure, and allows those of us in the community to see new topics and perspectives we may not have otherwise come across." Also an explicit invitation for teachers to help provide feedback via a short form.
